sources.content: Tupolev Tu-154M landing Mikhalis Makarov/Shutterstock Russia's last commercial Tupolev Tu-154 was finally retired from service in 2020, almost half a century after the first one left the factory. Production of the jet began in 1972, just as the then-Soviet Union's domestic aviation industry was starting to rapidly expand. The Tu-154 formed a vital part of that expansion, and was a common sight in the country's skies all the way through to the 2000s. sources.content: Linear pricing is a pricing strategy where price increases or decreases in direct proportion to the quantity of goods or services purchased. This type of pricing is common in businesses that sell commodities or other undifferentiated products. While linear pricing is straightforward and easy to understand, it can often be perceived as unfair by customers. This is because customers who purchase more of a product are effectively subsidizing the cost for those who purchase less. Linear pricing can also be difficult to sustain in cases where the cost of production decreases with increased output. Despite these challenges, linear pricing remains a popular pricing strategy due to [...] ## What is Linear Pricing? supported_claims.text: Linear offers a free plan that caps usage at two teams and 250 active issues while allowing unlimited members, and it includes core issue tracking, cycles, projects, and roadmaps.
Linear's Basic tier costs $10 per user per month with annual billing and includes unlimited issues, guest access, advanced filtering, and integrations.
Linear's Business tier costs $16 per user per month with annual billing and adds priority support, advanced analytics, SAML SSO, and SCIM provisioning.
Linear's Enterprise plan uses custom pricing and includes dedicated support, advanced security, and compliance features.
According to Spendflo, Linear pricing plans range from $5,000 to $70,000 depending on organizational needs.
Factors that affect Linear pricing include the number of teams, required features, and organization size, with discounts available for annual billing.
Guest accounts require Linear's Business plan and are billed as regular members rather than at a reduced rate.
Some Linear AI features, including coding sessions and loops, consume prepaid AI credits, while the remainder of its AI capabilities are included in standard plans.
Plane's managed cloud service starts at $6 per user per month when billed annually.
Plane's 10-seat Pro plan costs roughly 40% less than Linear's Basic tier.
GitHub's Team plan is priced at $4 per user per month.
GitHub's Enterprise plan starts at $21 per user per month.
Plane offers a free self-hosted tier with no per-seat cost for teams running the software on their own infrastructure.
Linear is intentionally narrow and built for Engineering, Product, and Design teams that want a polished, cloud-hosted service with minimal configuration.
Linear offers an interface optimized for keyboard navigation, automated sprint management, and streamlined design.
Plane serves Engineering, Marketing, Operations, and Customer Success teams, while Linear targets only Engineering, Product, and Design workflows.
Plane is an open-source alternative that supports self-hosting via Docker, and Codegen describes its codebase as MIT-licensed.
According to Zoobbe, Plane is licensed under AGPL-3.0.
Plane mirrors Linear's core model by using cycles for sprints, modules for epics, and a keyboard-driven interface.
Codegen states that Plane's interface is improving but still falls behind Linear in the refinement of keyboard shortcuts and overall responsiveness.
Plane provides a spreadsheet view for bulk-editing issues in a table format, a capability reviewers say is not natively matched by Linear or Jira.
Plane includes integrated pages tied to projects, which means teams may not need a separate wiki tool for specifications and meeting notes.
Hosted Huly has been discontinued and is no longer funded or available, though the software can still be self-hosted.
Huly is an open-source platform licensed under EPL-2.0 that combines project tracking, documents, team chat, video calls, and file management.
Huly includes two-way GitHub synchronization, built-in video conferencing, and collaborative wiki documents.
Huly runs multiple services in Docker containers and is described as more resource-intensive than simpler tools.
Huly offers syntax highlighting in code blocks for technical documentation.
GitHub Issues integrates tightly with code repositories and mixes timeline data with CI events, pull request reviews, and deployment notifications.
Linear's GitHub integration links issues to pull requests and commits and automatically updates issue status as pull requests move from drafted to merged.
Linear generates consistent issue identifiers that allow branches or pull requests containing those identifiers to automatically link back to the corresponding issue.
Linear maintains a detailed history of every state change, comment, and assignment, which supports automatic generation of standup summaries and sprint status reports.
DevToolReviews reports that Linear loads instantly and processes actions in under 100 milliseconds, using aggressive local caching and client-side updates that appear before server confirmation.
Jira offers maximum configurability for complex organizations.
Plane has a smaller integration ecosystem and more basic reporting and mobile experience than older tools, reflecting its newer market entry.
Alfred_ notes that Plane is the only major Linear alternative that allows full self-hosting on a team's own servers at no cost.
Linear provides an agent platform and an official MCP server.
Linear Agent launched in public beta on March 24, 2026, and can be assigned to issues, added to projects, and used to triage tasks and draft project updates.
Linear introduced Shared Skills on June 4, 2026, allowing teams to save and reuse agent instructions.
Linear's Coding Sessions became generally available on June 11, 2026, on Basic, Business, and Enterprise plans and allow the agent to generate code using Claude Code and Codex.
Linear earned a reputation for being the fastest and most opinionated issue tracker available.
Agiflow states that Linear is a best-in-class product development system with strong capabilities in cycles, triage, insights, roadmaps, and product operations.
Bundl rated Linear 4.7 out of 5 in August 2026 and described it as the default modern issue tracker for product-engineering teams that prioritize speed.
A Bundl review cited the free plan's 250-issue cap and annual-only paid billing as the main drawbacks.
